audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Jacob's embalming/mourning, Machpelah burial, brothers' fear, Joseph's providence statement, forgiveness, Joseph's death, and oath concerning bones.

verses.restored: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.

familiar.text: And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept upon him, and kissed him.

verses.restored: Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel.

familiar.text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Israel.

verses.restored: Forty days were fulfilled for him, for so are the days fulfilled for embalming, and Egypt wept for him seventy days.

familiar.text: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.

verses.restored: When the days of weeping for him had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s house, saying, If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in Pharaoh’s ears.

familiar.text: And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spake unto the house of Pharaoh, saying, If now I have found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

verses.restored: My father made me swear, saying, Look, I am dying; in my burial place that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me. Now please let me go up and bury my father, and I will return.

familiar.text: My father made me swear, saying, Lo, I die: in my grave which I have digged for me in the land of Canaan, there shalt thou bury me. Now therefore let me go up, I pray thee, and bury my father, and I will come again.

verses.restored: Pharaoh said, Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.

familiar.text: And Pharaoh said, Go up, and bury thy father, according as he made thee swear.

verses.restored: Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went all Pharaoh’s servants, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt.

familiar.text: And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

verses.restored: All Joseph’s house, his brothers, and his father’s house went up; only their little ones, flocks, and herds they left in Goshen.

familiar.text: And all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house: only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

verses.restored: Both chariots and horsemen went up with him; it was a very heavy camp.

familiar.text: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen: and it was a very great company.

verses.restored: They came to the threshing floor of Atad beyond the Jordan, and there they mourned with a very great and heavy mourning; he made mourning for his father seven days.

familiar.text: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

verses.restored: The Canaanite inhabitants of the land saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said, This is a heavy mourning for Egypt. Therefore its name was called Abel-mizraim, beyond the Jordan.

familiar.text: And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abelmizraim, which is beyond Jordan.

verses.restored: His sons did for him just as he had commanded them.

familiar.text: And his sons did unto him according as he commanded them:

verses.restored: His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought with the field as a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

familiar.text: For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

verses.restored: After burying his father, Joseph returned to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father.

familiar.text: And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brethren, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

verses.restored: Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead and said, Perhaps Joseph will hate us and fully repay us all the evil that we did to him.

familiar.text: And when Joseph’s brethren saw that their father was dead, they said, Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.

verses.restored: They sent a message to Joseph, saying, Your father commanded before his death, saying,

familiar.text: And they sent a messenger unto Joseph, saying, Thy father did command before he died, saying,

verses.restored: Thus you shall say to Joseph: Please forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they did evil to you. Now please forgive the transgression of the servants of the Divine of your father. Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

familiar.text: So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.

verses.restored: His brothers also went and fell before him and said, Look, we are your servants.

familiar.text: And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said, Behold, we be thy servants.

verses.restored: Joseph said to them, Do not fear, for am I in the place of the Divine?

familiar.text: And Joseph said unto them, Fear not: for am I in the place of God?

verses.restored: You planned evil against me; the Divine planned it for good, in order to do as this day, to keep many people alive.

familiar.text: But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

verses.restored: Now do not fear. I myself will sustain you and your little ones. He comforted them and spoke to their heart.

familiar.text: Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.

verses.restored: Joseph dwelled in Egypt, he and his father’s house, and Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

familiar.text: And Joseph dwelt in Egypt, he, and his father’s house: and Joseph lived an hundred and ten years.

verses.restored: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation; also the children of Machir son of Manasseh were born on Joseph’s knees.

familiar.text: And Joseph saw Ephraim’s children of the third generation: the children also of Machir the son of Manasseh were brought up upon Joseph’s knees.

verses.restored: Joseph said to his brothers, I am dying, but the Divine will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land he swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

familiar.text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

verses.restored: Joseph made the sons of Israel swear, saying, The Divine will surely visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from here.

familiar.text: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.

verses.restored: Joseph died, one hundred ten years old. They embalmed him, and he was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

familiar.text: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
